questionnaire.name: Street Connection Assessment – User Friendly
questionnaire.image_alt: #Crossroads with zebra crossings and a check mark

sections.title: Your point of view
sections.description: Select walking, cycling, or both. Questions will adapt to your selection.

questions.text: How do you move through this place? You can choose both answers.

options.text: Person walking or rolling (also with a stroller, cane, walker or wheelchair)
Person cycling or riding an e-scooter

questions.text: Which of these situations apply to your trip today?

options.text: Going to or from a bus, tram or metro stop
Going to or from a parked car
Going to or from bicycle parking
Accompanying a child (for example to school)
Using a wheelchair, walker, cane or other mobility aid

questions.text: How often do you use this place?

options.text: I avoid it or have stopped using it

sections.title: Quick assessment
sections.description: Answer these first. Then you can finish or add optional details.

questions.text: What kind of crossing or passage is this?
questions.help: A passage is any way to get across a road, a railway or a difference in level.

options.text: A street crossing (zebra crossing or intersection)
A bridge or footbridge over the road
An elevator, an escalator, a ramp or a few steps between two levels (a longer stairway is assessed as a street segment)

questions.text: How is this crossing controlled?

options.text: Zebra crossing without a traffic light
No zebra stripes and no traffic light

questions.text: Who is this crossing for?

options.text: There are separate markings for bicycles next to the pedestrian ones
Not marked for bicycles, but bicycles use it

questions.text: Which best describes using this place on foot?

options.text: I can pass without slowing down
I need to slow down a little
I need to be careful while passing
It takes a lot of effort or attention
I avoid using it if possible
I cannot get through (for example with a wheelchair or stroller)

questions.text: Because of traffic (cars, motorcycles, bicycles), how risky does it feel to use this place on foot?
Which best describes using this place by bicycle or e-scooter?

options.text: I can pass without slowing down
I need to slow down a little
I need to be careful while passing
It takes a lot of effort or attention
I avoid using it if possible
I cannot get through by bicycle or e-scooter

questions.text: Because of traffic, how risky does it feel to use this place by bicycle or e-scooter?
How safe from harassment or assault do you feel here, also in the evening?
questions.help: Harassment means unwanted comments, gestures or contact. This question is about your own feeling, not about traffic.

options.text: I do not go there in the evening

questions.text: What happens at the traffic light when you cross?
questions.help: Turning cars are vehicles that turn at the junction and drive across the crossing while the light for people crossing is green. Who should go refers to the right of way, that is who is allowed to go first.

options.text: Traffic light: when it is green for me, the cars are stopped
Traffic light, but turning cars still pass
There is a traffic light, but it is unclear who should go
The traffic light is broken or switched off

questions.text: Is there a refuge island where people can stop between traffic lanes?
Would you like to add more details? There are about 10 to 22 optional questions, depending on the place and on how you move (about 3–7 minutes).

sections.title: Access and crossing
sections.description: Look at the place. Answer only what you can see.

questions.text: Can people on foot use this place?

options.text: Yes, but not with a wheelchair or stroller
Yes, but it is hard to understand where to go
No, it is closed or forbidden
No, it is not possible to get through

questions.text: Can people pass through this place by bicycle or e-scooter?

options.text: Yes, with a dedicated bicycle space
Yes, but you need to get off and push the bicycle
No, it is not possible to get through by bicycle or e-scooter

questions.text: By bicycle or e-scooter, what problems do you find at this crossing?

options.text: The cycle path stops before or after the crossing
There is no crossing for bicycles: people use the zebra crossing
Cars do not give way to bicycles
Cars or motorcycles stopped on the cycle path near the crossing
A curb or step at the entrance of the cycle path
The cycle path is not physically separated from motor traffic

questions.text: Which elements are part of this place?
Today, is the elevator working?

options.text: No, the elevator is broken or out of service
No, the elevator is closed (by a gate or at certain hours)

questions.text: Today, is the escalator working?

options.text: No, the escalator is broken or stopped
No, the escalator is closed (by a gate or at certain hours)

questions.text: How do you get the green light to cross?

options.text: It comes by itself, every cycle
You have to press the button, and it works
There is a button, but it does not work

questions.text: Does the traffic light have a sound signal for people who cannot see?

options.text: Yes, but it does not work or can barely be heard

questions.text: How many traffic lanes must people cross here?
questions.help: A traffic lane is a strip of road for one line of moving vehicles. Bus lanes count, parking spaces do not.

questions.text: Before crossing, can you clearly see approaching vehicles or bicycles, also at the height of a child or a wheelchair user?
What blocks the view?

options.text: Parked or stopped cars or vans
Signs, poles, boxes, or street furniture

questions.text: Can people clearly see the path and the exit?

options.text: Yes, the path and exit are clearly visible
No, there are blind corners or hidden areas

sections.title: Orientation and space
sections.description: Look at the place. Answer only what you can see.

questions.text: How easy is it to understand where people should go?
Why is it difficult to understand?
questions.help: Markings are lines and symbols painted on the ground. Signs are on poles or walls.

options.text: The crossing or passage is hard to recognize
It is not clear if people can walk here
It is not clear if people can cycle here

questions.text: Is there enough safe space to wait before crossing or to stop and rest?

options.text: A place exists, but it is too small
No space to wait or rest is needed here

questions.text: Who might find it hard or impossible to use this place?

options.text: People using a walker or walking aid
Children (for example walking alone to school)
People who walk slowly or need more time (for example older people)
People who find it hard to find their way or understand signs

sections.title: Safety features and condition
sections.description: Look at the place. Answer only what you can see.

questions.text: What helps people use this place safely?
questions.help: Tactile paving is a ridged or dotted ground surface that blind or visually impaired people can feel with a cane or their feet.

options.text: Raised crossing (at the same level as the sidewalk)
Different color or material on the ground
Protected island or safe place to stop
Traffic light with a sound signal
Countdown showing the remaining green time
Markings or colored surface for bicycles

questions.text: What problems do you see at this crossing?

options.text: The stripes are faded or worn away
There is a curb ramp, but cars or motorcycles park in front of it
The curb ramp is broken or has a step to the road
Cars or motorcycles parked on the crossing
Cobblestones, potholes or damaged paving on the crossing
The cycle path cuts across the sidewalk: bicycles and pedestrians cross paths

questions.text: What problems do you see in this underpass?

options.text: Walls or ceiling in poor condition
Few people pass, it feels isolated
Long, with only one entrance and one exit

questions.text: Is this bridge covered?
For stairs, what helps people use them?
questions.help: A bike rail or channel is a groove at the side of the steps for pushing a bicycle.

questions.text: What problems do the stairs have?

options.text: Closed by a gate or at certain hours

questions.text: How many steps are there?

options.text: A few steps, up to about 10

questions.text: For a ramp, what helps people use it?

options.text: Wide enough for wheelchairs or strollers

questions.text: Is the ramp too steep for a wheelchair or stroller?

sections.title: Your experience here
sections.description: Answer based on your experience. Walking and cycling questions appear according to your selection.

questions.text: When there is no working traffic light, how often do drivers stop to let people cross?
At the traffic light, how long do you usually wait for green?
Does the green light last long enough to cross calmly?

options.text: No, the light turns red before I finish crossing

questions.text: How often do you see dangerous behaviour here by people walking, cycling or driving?
Which situations do you observe?
questions.help: The marked place is the zebra crossing or the official passage.

options.text: Cars or motorcycles do not stop at the zebra crossing
Vehicles go through the red light
Motorcycles or e-scooters ride on the sidewalk
Motorcycles and mopeds weaving between stopped cars while people cross
People cross outside the marked place
People cross against the red light
Vehicles stop or park on the crossing or passage

sections.title: Improve this place
sections.description: Tell us whether improving this place should be a priority.

questions.text: How urgent is it to improve this place?
What would improve this place most?

options.text: Longer green light for people crossing
A new or repaired traffic light
A zebra crossing where it is missing
Sound signal at the traffic light for people who cannot see
More visible signs or markings (where they already exist)
Protect the crossing and curb ramp from parking (for example with bollards)
Safer space to wait or rest
Curb ramps, ramps or working elevators
Changes that make vehicles go slower
Connect the cycle path from one side of the crossing to the other

questions.text: Anything else you want to add?
questions.help: Please do not write names or other personal data.

questions.text: What kind of crossing or passage is this?
questions.help: A passage is any way to get across a road, a railway or a difference in level.

options.text: A street crossing (zebra crossing or intersection)
A bridge or footbridge over the road
An elevator, an escalator, a ramp or a few steps between two levels (a longer stairway is assessed as a street segment)
